parts: When did Pompeii end? One scribble pointed to October.
It was found in October twenty eighteen.
It reads: the sixteenth day before the Kalends of November.
Our arithmetic: Roman counting makes that October seventeenth.
The Ministry of Culture reasoned that charcoal is fragile.
So it was most likely written in October of seventy-nine.
So the park tested it, on the same wall, under a rain cover.
The park reports it was essentially unaltered after ten months. Still perfectly legible.
Our reading: it does not prove August. It weakens one argument against it.
